invariants: Tests never write into the source tree: a run that did (v0.3.0) counted a file a test wrote as a passing test.
A step the player does not know fails; it is never skipped.
A program that ends with steps left fails (STEPS NOT FINISHED): the steps not run were never checked.

The Qt dialect checks the tool tip box (v0.9.0: expect tipShown|tipText|tipTitle|tipLines|tipWidthSet|tipAtClient|tipBesideItem) and the program's output after it ends (output lines|count TEXT ==> WANT, checked by the runner).

The Qt dialect (v0.8.0) checks layouts against a mark: marklayout, then expect delta|right|scaled|unchanged|limits; and month calendars: mcpick, expect mcTitle|mcBold|mcBoldIn|mcSel|mcSelShown|mcFits.
As in the browser harness, a program may return a value once its output matches its .expect; a Rexx error, a failed step, or a non-zero return without an .expect fails it.

A sweep verdict of SHOWN means a dialog came up with no Rexx error, nothing more; MODULE files (required by another file) are listed, not started; programs whose header says to run them from the parent folder are run so.
Every run is killed after 90 seconds, so a hang shows as a failure.

The Qt dialect (v0.12.0) checks what a program hands to the user and its window (expect delivered|deliveredItem|deliverActions|deliverPanels, and pdf K ==> PAGES ; text ; ... through poppler's pdfinfo and pdftotext, fragments in order), and the status bar, rows and colours (stbDocked, stbText, stbPartWidths, stbPartText, stbPartTip, lvRows, lvFirsts, clientBg, buttonTexts, counts, lvColors).

The Qt dialect (v0.13.0) checks the tool bar (tbDocked, tbButtons, tbPushed, tbDisabled N, scope .ood-tb >> text=), custom draw as the page's computed style reads it (lvCd R [font], tvCd TEXT: text colour on background [font family]), tvKids TEXT, lvCount, and scrolls a view to its end with scrollend SELECTOR.

The Qt dialect (v0.14.0) checks the re-bar (rbDocked, rbBands, rbLayout, rbColors, rbFirst, rbCount; scope .ood-rb with >> text=, select, input) and whether a dialog is within reach (dlgReach: in, top-left, out); screenarea W H stands in for the browser's viewport step, and screenarea 0 0 restores the screen's own area.
procedure: Build: cmake and make in native/ (see the README's Build section).
Add --shots DIR and look at the screenshots: geometry defects (a highlighted row the program did not select, a strip lost under a layout) pass the checks and show only there.

provenance.claim: Fresh staging directory, as /home/rexx, with Windows names.

summary: Three ooRexx tools share one runner class, tools/OodQtTest.cls, and log through oorexx_logging (ToolProgress). tools/oodqt_test.rex runs given tests. tools/oodqt_suite.rex runs the whole suite in the browser harness's groups: designer and res with no tree; t* and up with upstream's samples/windows/oodialog; up2 with samples/tutorial; up3 with samples/propertysheet.tabControls; up4 with samples/mouse; up5 with samples/controls/ListView/subitem.editing; up6 SimpleMonthCalendar with samples/simple and PaidHolidays with samples/controls; up7 with samples/resizableDialogs/ResizingAdmin; up8 with samples/controls/ToolTip; up9 with samples/propertysheet.tabControls; up10 customDrawListview with samples/controls/ListView and treeViewCustomDraw with samples/controls/TreeView; print with the --pdfkit directory (oodialog-wasm's tools/oodpdfkit.rex output), left out without it. A file a test hands to the user (deliver) goes to the test's own staged directory (OODQT_DELIVER), so it is removed with it. tools/oodqt_sweep.rex starts every upstream sample with nothing clicked and writes a Markdown report. Each program runs in a fresh directory under TMPDIR, as the page runs it in a fresh /home/rexx. The directory holds the program, its TEST.files/, the --tree, ooDialog.cls, oodWeb.cls and ooShapes.cls, plus the Windows file names the program uses (tools/WindowsNames.cls, a port of the page's oodfiles.js; since 0.2.0 also data files named in strings). In .steps and .expect, /home/rexx means that directory. The steps player runs inside the Qt loop. It takes the harness's verbs (wait, click, fill, select, press, type, mouse, sleep, shot, expect) and Playwright-style selectors, and translates the harness's JavaScript checks it knows; it fails any step it does not know. Where a test's checks are JavaScript the player cannot translate, tests/steps/NAME.qt.steps gives the same steps in a Qt dialect. --platform xcb runs everything on an X server (under xvfb-run, or a desktop's DISPLAY).
title: Testing: the browser harness's own tests, the designer's programs, and a sweep of every sample
